headline: Sales grow, margins compress, guidance held
summary_short: Home Depot's fiscal Q1 2026 (three months ended May 3, 2026) sales rose 4.8% y/y to $41.8B, but GAAP diluted EPS fell 4.3% to $3.30 as operating margin compressed to 11.9% from 12.9%. The company reaffirmed its full fiscal-2026 guidance.
summary_long: Sales rose 4.8% y/y to $41.8B; total-company comparable sales grew 0.6% (U.S. +0.4%) despite ongoing consumer uncertainty and housing-affordability pressure, per CEO Ted Decker. SG&A and depreciation grew 5.7%, outpacing sales, so GAAP operating income fell 3.0% to $4.98B and operating margin compressed to 11.9% from 12.9%; adjusted operating margin (ex. SRS intangible amortization) was 12.3% vs 13.2%. Diluted EPS was $3.30, down 4.3%; adjusted EPS was $3.43, down 3.7%. Operating cash flow rose 39% to $6.0B; capex was $844M. Cash fell to $1.6B after $1.4B of debt repayment and $2.3B of dividends paid. The company reaffirmed its full fiscal-2026 guidance across sales, margin, tax-rate, and EPS growth.

drivers.explanation: Demand was "relatively similar" to fiscal 2025 despite "greater consumer uncertainty and housing affordability pressure," per CEO Ted Decker; associates delivered steady customer service.
Comparable sales rose 0.6% (U.S. +0.4%); FX added roughly 55bp to total-company comparable sales, on top of the sales contribution from SRS/GMS.
SG&A plus depreciation together grew 5.7% versus 4.8% sales growth, which arithmetically compresses operating margin even before any single disclosed cause.
Acquired-intangible amortization tied to the SRS acquisition rose to $171M from $139M, a disclosed reconciling item between GAAP and adjusted operating income.
EPS decline is fully explained by lower net earnings (-4.2%) against a roughly flat diluted share count (+0.2% y/y).
